page: Hetzner Cloud ccx13 is a dedicated CPU virtual server built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 8.0 GB of RAM, which equates to approximately 3.91 GB per core, and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and virtualization is managed via QEMU.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is strong, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory performance is also constrained, with a poor PassMark memory score and read-only small block memory bandwidth in the bottom 10%, though large block write bandwidth remains in the average range. Real-world application benchmarks reflect these limitations, showing weak performance in Redis SET operations, static web serving, and software compilation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx13 offers dedicated CPU resources at an entry-level hardware profile, making it a viable option for workloads requiring predictable CPU allocation without the overhead of high-density instances. Given the strong single-core performance but limited multi-core and memory bandwidth, this server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, small-scale web serving, or minor LLM text generation tasks using very small models. It is less suitable for database operations, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or memory-intensive workloads.
